sentences.text:
The instant writ petition has been filed praying for the following relief:
"i. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus directing the Respondent No. 2, the District Magistrate/Collector, Ghazipur, to decide the Petitioners' pending application dated 01.02.2024 in accordance with law within a stipulated period; and ii. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus Directing the Respondent No. 4, the Executive Engineer, Devkali Pump Canal,
Second Division, Ghazipur, to determine and pay compensation to the Petitioners for the affected area being Arazi No. 54/2, measuring 0.1010 hectare, in accordance with the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013;."
3.

entities.text: to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are the rightful and transferable owners of the disputed land.
A portion of their land being Arazi No.54/2, measuring 0.1010 hectares, was acquired for the construction of residential colony and road purposes.
However, no compensation has been paid to them.

Despite multiple representations, including one dated 30.01.2024 addressed to the Executive Engineer, Devkali Pump Canal, Second Division, Ghazipur,
for removal of the unauthorized construction, no action has been taken.

At the outset, he has placed reliance on the Division Bench Judgment in Writ C No.12698 of 2025 (Dalip Singh and 4 others vs.
State of U.P. and 3 others).
4.

entities.text:
Dalip Singh and 4 others vs.
State of U.P. and 3 others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel has raised a preliminary objection regarding the maintainability of the writ petition,

He further submits that the matter involves highly disputed facts that cannot be adjudicated in a writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India and that the High Court should not relegate such matters for adjudication in a civil court.
He also states that nothing has been placed on record to substantiate that the petitioners have a substantial right to raise this claim after more than five decades of the construction.

In support of his submissions, he relies on the judgment and order dated 04.04.2011 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal Nos. 2913-2914 of 2011 (Syed Maqbool Ali vs. State of U.P. and Another), reported in (2011)
4 SCR 238.

sentences.text: Having considered the factual matrix of the case and the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Syed Maqbool Ali vs. State of U.P. and Another, (2011) 4 SCR 238, we are of the considered opinion that no interference is warranted in the exercise of writ jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

entities.text: Syed Maqbool Ali vs. State of U.P. and Another, (2011) 4 SCR 238
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said decision, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that where land is alleged to have been taken without acquisition, a writ petition may be maintainable only if the action of the State is arbitrary, unreasonable, or without authority of law.

However, the Apex Court also cautioned that claims raised after several decades, without satisfactory explanation for the delay,
and involving disputed questions of fact, are not amenable to writ jurisdiction and should ordinarily be relegated to the appropriate civil forum.

Applying the principles laid down in the aforesaid case to the present matter, and in the absence of any cogent explanation for the long delay or substantiation of legal right, we are not inclined to grant the relief sought by the petitioners.

6. Consequently, this Court is of the opinion that the petitioners ought to pursue their remedy, if any, before the appropriate civil forum, where such factual disputes can be properly adjudicated on the basis of evidence.
For the reasons stated above, we dispose of the instant petition in terms of Dalip Singh (supra).
(Kunal Ravi Singh,J.) (Mahesh Chandra Tripathi,J.) November 6, 2025
